app.name: Furca
app.tagline: A fast git client that stays out of your way.

splash.tip: Drop a folder on the window to open the repository in it.

open.lineHint: Every repository rigger records, read fresh each time

session.title: Save the open tabs
session.name: Name
session.help: Opening the session later brings back these tabs, in this order.
session.replaces: A session of this name is saved already: this replaces it.

home.title: No repository open
home.body: Open one, pick one you had open lately, or drop a folder on the window.

column.label: Branches, remotes, tags, stashes and submodules

graph.label: Commits
graph.emptyBody: The first commit made here shows up in this place.
graph.inMessageHint: nooma found the words in the body of the commit message

standing.operationBody: git started it and has not finished: continue or abort it in a terminal.

views.label: What to show of the repository

release.label: Release
release.noneBody: A repository is released from its release.toml, and this one has none.
release.listLabel: The checks of the plan and the steps of the run
release.notReadyBody: Red stops the release, as it does in the terminal. Mend it, then plan again.
release.underWayBody: Resume carries it on from {{next}}. It cannot start over: what is pushed stays.
release.failed: The release could not go on
release.nothingToSay: This step has nothing to say yet.
release.confirmBody: Past the gate this pushes, tags and publishes, and a tag that went out stays. Keep the window open: closing it stops the run where it is.

changes.failed: Could not read the working copy
changes.cleanBody: The working tree is exactly what HEAD holds. Files you save show up here as they change.
changes.more_one: and {{count}} more: furca status lists it
changes.more_other: and {{count}} more: furca status lists them all
changes.conflictTitle: A merge left this file unresolved: {{kind}}
changes.conflictBody: Settle it with git in a terminal; the file leaves this list as soon as it is staged.
changes.pickHint: Click line numbers to pick lines
changes.discardBody: Nothing keeps a copy: a change that was never staged, committed or stashed is gone for good.

composer.label: The commit to make
composer.breakingHint: Marks the commit with a ! before the colon: it breaks something for whoever uses this
composer.description: What it does, in a line
composer.body: Why, if the line cannot say it
composer.pushed: The last commit has been pushed: amending it rewrites what others may have.
composer.asking: Claude Code is writing a draft
composer.draftHint: Sends what is staged to the Claude Code CLI on this machine, and puts its draft in the form to read and change
composer.draftOver: Clear the message first: a draft does not write over what you typed
composer.doctorLabel: What is worth a word before this is committed

doctor.endings_one: {{count}} file ends its lines another way, which reads as every line changed
doctor.endings_other: {{count}} files end their lines another way, which reads as every line changed
doctor.large_one: {{count}} large file, which every clone carries for good
doctor.large_other: {{count}} large files, which every clone carries for good
doctor.assistant_one: {{count}} assistant's file is going into the repository
doctor.assistant_other: {{count}} assistant's files are going into the repository

finding.notConventional: Not a Conventional Commit: the release engine will not read what kind of change this is.
finding.unknownType: {{name}} is not a type of the convention.
finding.noBlankLine: The second line should be blank: git takes it as more of the subject.
finding.longSubject: The subject is {{length}} characters; {{most}} is the most that reads well.
finding.finalPeriod: The subject ends in a full stop.
finding.notEnglish: The message is not in English.

console.title: Console
console.label: The runs of git made here
console.toggle: Show what git this window has run
console.empty: git has not been run here yet
console.emptyBody: Reads go through gitoxide. What changes a repository runs git, and shows up here as you could have typed it.

status.unwatched: Not watching the working tree: it is read when the window gets the focus
status.writingGraph: git is writing the commit-graph, so the history opens fast…
status.wroteGraph: git wrote the commit-graph in {{seconds}} s
status.graphFailed: git could not write the commit-graph: {{reason}}

shell.broken: The window could not read what it had open

details.noneBody: Choose a commit in the graph to see what it changed.
details.noFilesBody: This commit changes nothing against its first parent.
details.resizeDetails: Resize the graph and the commit's details
details.resizeFiles: Resize the changed files and the diff
details.toParent: Go to this parent in the graph
details.diffFailed: Could not read this file's change
details.binaryBody: git does not compare it by lines. Committed as it is, every version of it stays in the repository's history for good.
details.lfsBody: The commit holds a pointer; the file lives in LFS storage.
details.submoduleBody: The commit moved the submodule to another of its commits.
details.drawFailedBody: The rest of the window is unaffected. Choose another file, or try again.

stash.button: Put every change away, untracked files too
stash.nothing: Nothing to stash: the working tree is what HEAD holds
stash.title: Stash changes
stash.body: Puts away {{changed}} and {{untracked}}, staged or not, and leaves the working tree as HEAD has it.
stash.bodyUnknown: Puts away every change, staged or not, and untracked files, and leaves the working tree as HEAD has it.
stash.messageHelp: What to know it by in the list; git names it after the branch without one.
stash.entryBody: A stash entry, with everything it put away
stash.applyHelp: Apply it to the working tree and keep it
stash.popHelp: Apply it and drop it; one that meets a conflict is kept
stash.dropBody: "{{message}}" goes out of the stash without being applied, and nothing in the window names it again.

reach.fetchHelp: Fetch every remote: their branches and tags as they are now
reach.pullHelp: Pull {{upstream}} into this branch, as your git is configured to
reach.pullRebase: Pull, rebasing your commits on top
reach.pushNew: Push {{branch}}, which follows nothing yet, and follow it from then on
reach.forceBody: {{branch}} on {{remote}} is replaced with this one, as long as it still holds what the last fetch saw there: {{lost}}. If someone pushed since, git refuses and nothing is lost.
reach.lost_zero: it has nothing this branch does not, so nothing goes
reach.lost_one: the {{count}} commit there that this branch does not have goes
reach.lost_other: the {{count}} commits there that this branch does not have go
reach.noRemotes: This repository has no remote yet
reach.noUpstream: {{branch}} follows no remote branch yet: push it, and it will

failed.remove: git did not remove the remote
failed.checkout: git did not check it out
failed.unfollow: git did not change what the branch follows
failed.push-tag: git did not push the tag
failed.delete-tag: The tag was not taken away everywhere

reach.failedSome: Pushed to {{remotes}}, and not to the rest
reach.pushedFollowing: Pushed {{branch}} to {{remotes}}; it follows {{remote}} from now on

remote.addBody: A name for it and its address. Its branches are fetched once it is added; your git's credential helper or ssh-agent answers for it.
remote.editBody: Renaming it moves its remote-tracking branches, and the branches that follow it follow it under the new name. A password kept in the address is not shown, and stays unless you change the address.
remote.name: Name
remote.removeBody: Its remote-tracking branches go from this repository, and the branches that follow {{name}} follow nothing. Nothing on the remote itself is touched.

refs.deleteHead: HEAD is on this branch: check out another one first
refs.name: Name
refs.nameHelp: A slash makes a folder: feature/login
refs.branchAlone: It follows nothing until its first push, and then its own name on the remote it went to.
refs.branchFollows: Named {{name}}, it follows {{from}}; under any other name it follows nothing until its first push.
refs.renameBody: What it follows and its history of moves go with it.
refs.followBody: Pull brings what is new on the branch it follows, and Push sends it there.
refs.noRemoteBranches: There are no remote branches here yet: fetch a remote first.
refs.deleteCounting: Counting the commits only it holds…
refs.deleteBody_zero: Every commit on it is on another branch or tag as well, so nothing is lost. It was at {{at}}.
refs.deleteBody_one: The commit only it holds goes with it: no other branch or tag has it. git keeps it in its reflog for a while. It was at {{at}}.
refs.deleteBody_other: The {{count}} commits only it holds go with it: no other branch or tag has them. git keeps them in its reflog for a while. It was at {{at}}.
refs.tagMessageHelp: With a message it is an annotated tag, which a push of its branch takes along. Without one it is a bookmark, which stays here until it is pushed by name.
refs.deleteTagBody: It goes from this repository. A remote that has it gives it back on the next fetch: tick the ones to take it away from too.
refs.checkedOutFollowing: Checked out {{branch}}, a new branch following {{upstream}}
refs.checkedOutDetached: HEAD is on {{at}}, on no branch
refs.deletedBranch_one: Deleted {{name}}, which was at {{at}}, and the commit only it held
refs.deletedBranch_other: Deleted {{name}}, which was at {{at}}, and the {{count}} commits only it held
refs.deletedTagThere: Deleted the tag {{tag}} here and from {{remotes}}
